blocks.x: One crying-wolf quarter kills the program; alarm governance is a first-class design goal.
Predictive maintenance fails socially before it fails statistically. Failure-mode-driven models beat generic anomaly detection — physics before ML.
Predictions must become work orders with parts reserved, or they are dashboard decorations.
Planner trust (share of predictions actioned) is the KPI that predicts program survival.
Where this goes wrong in practice
Applied carelessly, it breaks the same way every time — the demo gap: pilots on curated feeds, production on messy reality — and a twin that drifts from the asset until operators stop opening it.

The strongest counter-case, stated fairly: the twin-first thesis can produce beautiful models of assets nobody needed simulated. The twin earns its keep on the decisions it changes, not the fidelity it displays.
The practice, as we run it

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: we connect machines, fleets and facilities into one operational picture, then close the loop into maintenance, scheduling and control. Every program in the IoT, Twin & Robotics domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
If predictive maintenance fails socially before it fails statistically is on your agenda this year, a briefing will tell you in 45 minutes whether this pattern fits your estate.
